claim: Skeletal muscle comprises 40% of total body mass.
source: Skeletal muscle is a unique tissue that comprises 40% of our total body mass and is essential for breathing, movement, and metabolism.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion in the introduction without specific experimental data from this study, drawing on established scientific knowledge.

claim: A single skeletal muscle fiber contains hundreds of nuclei.
source: In contrast to the majority of other cell types, a single skeletal muscle fiber, which is formed from the fusion of precursor cells during development, contains hundreds of nuclei (Deng et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Deng et al., 2017.

claim: Muscle has the ability to regenerate due to the presence of muscle stem cells (MuSCs or satellite cells).
source: Muscle is a remarkably plastic tissue in the adult with the ability to regenerate due to the presence of bona fide muscle stem cells (MuSCs or also referred to as satellite cells), and also respond to various stimuli by altering its contractile and metabolic properties (Egan and Zierath, 2013; Hoppeler, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Egan and Zierath, 2013 and Hoppeler, 2016.

claim: MuSCs are activated in humans after exercise.
source: There is consensus that MuSCs are indeed activated in humans after exercise, however whether MuSC activation and downstream myonuclear accretion is required for adaptive hypertrophy is not fully understood (Snijders et al., 2015; Murach et al., 2018a; Bamman et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Snijders et al., 2015; Murach et al., 2018a; and Bamman et al., 2018.

claim: Growth of 18% in slow, type I myofibers is associated with an increase of myonuclei.
source: The requirement of myonuclear accretion for hypertrophy may depend on muscle fiber type as growth of 18% in slow, type I myofibers is associated with an increase of myonuclei (Snijders et al., 2016; Bellamy et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Snijders et al., 2016 and Bellamy et al., 2014.

claim: An increase in myonuclear content of fast, type II myofibers is only observed after 26–40% hypertrophy.
source: In contrast, an increase in myonuclear content of fast, type II myofibers is only observed after 26–40% hypertrophy (Snijders et al., 2016; Kadi et al., 2004; Petrella et al., 2006; Stec et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Snijders et al., 2016; Kadi et al., 2004; Petrella et al., 2006; and Stec et al., 2016.

claim: Synergist ablation is an invasive procedure where a synergist muscle is surgically removed leaving a smaller muscle to do all of the required work.
source: Muscle overload by synergist ablation is the most often used stimulus to drive hypertrophy in the mouse, however it is an invasive procedure where a synergist muscle (e.g., gastrocnemius) is surgically removed leaving a smaller muscle (e.g., plantaris) to do all of the required work to ambulate the limb (Kirby et al., 2016a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kirby et al., 2016a.

claim: MP fusion is required for synergist ablation at young ages (below 4 months of age) but not at older timepoints.
source: Current ideas include that MP fusion is required for synergist ablation at young ages (below 4 months of age) but not at older timepoints (Murach et al., 2017a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Murach et al., 2017a.

claim: Abrogation of MP fusion by genetically deleting Myomaker resulted in significantly blunted synergist ablation-induced hypertrophy.
source: Through a complementary approach, we abrogated MP fusion by genetically deleting Myomaker (Mymk), a muscle-specific factor required for fusion, and found that synergist ablation-induced hypertrophy was significantly blunted (Goh and Millay, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work (Goh and Millay, 2017).

claim: Ablation of MuSCs by DTA has minimal impact on adaptations to voluntary wheel running.
source: While voluntary wheel running is a standard exercise stimulus for the mouse and ablation of MuSCs by DTA have minimal impact on adaptations to voluntary wheel running (Jackson et al., 2015; Murach et al., 2017b), this exercise stimulus does not lead to significant myofiber hypertrophy (De Lisio and Farup, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jackson et al., 2015 and Murach et al., 2017b.

claim: Voluntary wheel running does not lead to significant myofiber hypertrophy.
source: While voluntary wheel running is a standard exercise stimulus for the mouse and ablation of MuSCs by DTA have minimal impact on adaptations to voluntary wheel running (Jackson et al., 2015; Murach et al., 2017b), this exercise stimulus does not lead to significant myofiber hypertrophy (De Lisio and Farup, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to De Lisio and Farup, 2017.

claim: A progressive weighted wheel running protocol was recently reported to increase myofiber size.
source: A progressive weighted wheel running protocol was recently reported to increase myofiber size but it is not understood if this exercise regimen is associated with improved muscle function or if MP fusion is required (Dungan et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dungan et al., 2019.

claim: Initiation of an exercise regimen leads to mechanical damage of the muscle characterized by alterations of the cytoskeleton and structural proteins.
source: Indeed, initiation of an exercise regimen leads to mechanical damage of the muscle characterized by alterations of the cytoskeleton and structural proteins (Damas et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Damas et al., 2018.

claim: The 8-week HIIT protocol led to a significant increase in muscle weight of the gastrocnemius in 8-month-old wild-type mice.
source: Analysis of muscle weights revealed a significant increase of multiple muscle groups in HIIT-trained mice compared to sedentary mice (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B comparing muscle weights between sedentary and HIIT-trained mice.

claim: The 8-week HIIT protocol led to a significant increase in muscle weight of the quadriceps in 8-month-old wild-type mice.
source: Analysis of muscle weights revealed a significant increase of multiple muscle groups in HIIT-trained mice compared to sedentary mice (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B comparing muscle weights between sedentary and HIIT-trained mice.

claim: The 8-week HIIT protocol led to a significant increase in muscle weight of the tibialis anterior in 8-month-old wild-type mice.
source: Analysis of muscle weights revealed a significant increase of multiple muscle groups in HIIT-trained mice compared to sedentary mice (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B comparing muscle weights between sedentary and HIIT-trained mice.

claim: The 8-week HIIT protocol led to a significant increase in muscle weight of the extensor digitorum longus in 8-month-old wild-type mice.
source: Analysis of muscle weights revealed a significant increase of multiple muscle groups in HIIT-trained mice compared to sedentary mice (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B comparing muscle weights between sedentary and HIIT-trained mice.

claim: Peak isometric tetanic force of the hindlimb plantar flexor was increased after HIIT compared to sedentary mice.
source: Peak isometric tetanic force of the hindlimb plantar flexor was increased after HIIT compared to sedentary mice (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D measuring peak isometric tetanic force.

claim: HIIT resulted in an increase in rate of activation of hindlimb plantar flexor muscles.
source: We observed an increase in rate of activation (Figure 1E) but no significant effect on rate of relaxation (Figure 1F), indicating that HIIT-trained muscle has the capability to generate peak tetanic force more quickly.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E measuring rate of activation.

claim: HIIT had no significant effect on rate of relaxation of hindlimb plantar flexor muscles.
source: We observed an increase in rate of activation (Figure 1E) but no significant effect on rate of relaxation (Figure 1F), indicating that HIIT-trained muscle has the capability to generate peak tetanic force more quickly.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F measuring rate of relaxation.

claim: Calculation of impulse revealed an increase after HIIT showing that muscles can sustain higher force over a single contraction.
source: Finally, calculation of impulse (area under the peak isometric tetanic force curve) revealed an increase after HIIT showing that those muscles can sustain higher force over a single contraction (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G measuring impulse.

claim: Sedentary EDL myofibers contained 227 ± 15 myonuclei.
source: Quantification of the number of nuclei per myofiber revealed 227 ± 15 myonuclei from sedentary muscle, whereas myofibers after 2 weeks of HIIT contained 253 ± 11 myonuclei (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B quantifying nuclei per myofiber.

claim: EDL myofibers after 2 weeks of HIIT contained 253 ± 11 myonuclei.
source: Quantification of the number of nuclei per myofiber revealed 227 ± 15 myonuclei from sedentary muscle, whereas myofibers after 2 weeks of HIIT contained 253 ± 11 myonuclei (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B quantifying nuclei per myofiber.

claim: EDL myofibers after 4 weeks of HIIT contained 281 ± 9 myonuclei.
source: After 4 weeks of HIIT myofibers contained 281 ± 9 and at 8 weeks there were 306 ± 12 myonuclei (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B quantifying nuclei per myofiber.

claim: EDL myofibers after 8 weeks of HIIT contained 306 ± 12 myonuclei.
source: After 4 weeks of HIIT myofibers contained 281 ± 9 and at 8 weeks there were 306 ± 12 myonuclei (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B quantifying nuclei per myofiber.

claim: There is a continuous increase in myonuclei throughout the HIIT exercise regimen.
source: These data demonstrate that there is a continuous increase in myonuclei throughout the exercise regimen.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the progressive increase in myonuclear numbers shown in Figure 2B across different time points.

claim: Analysis of myonuclear number in quadriceps revealed an increase in myonuclei consistent with the analysis in EDL myofibers.
source: To complement the analysis of myonuclei in isolated EDL myofibers, we also assessed myonuclear number on cryosections from quadriceps by evaluating the number of nuclei within a dystrophin-stained myofiber. This analysis also revealed an increase in myonuclei (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), consistent with the analysis in EDL myofibers.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Different methods to quantify nuclear number (EDL myofibers vs quadriceps sections) yield similar results.
source: Moreover, analysis of the relative increase in myonuclei in the quadriceps and EDL showed that the different methods to quantify nuclear number yield similar results (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B comparing the two methods.

claim: Myofiber cross-sectional area significantly increased at 8 weeks but not at 2 or 4 weeks post-HIIT in the gastrocnemius.
source: Quantification of myofiber cross-sectional area (CSA) indeed showed a significant increase at 8 weeks but not at prior time points (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D quantifying myofiber CSA at different time points.

claim: Myofiber cross-sectional area significantly increased at 8 weeks but not at 2 or 4 weeks post-HIIT in the quadriceps.
source: Quantification of myofiber cross-sectional area (CSA) indeed showed a significant increase at 8 weeks but not at prior time points (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D quantifying myofiber CSA at different time points.

claim: Muscle hypertrophy occurs between 4 and 8 weeks of the HIIT protocol, which is delayed compared to the initiation of myonuclear addition.
source: Thus, muscle responds to HIIT by increasing cell size and this hypertrophy occurs between 4 and 8 weeks of the protocol, which is delayed compared to the initiation of myonuclear addition.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the data showing myonuclear accretion starting at 2 weeks (Figure 2B) but significant hypertrophy only at 8 weeks (Figure 2D).

claim: MyomakerscKO 8w mice exhibited a significant increase in the number of times they landed on the shock grid during HIIT, which progressively worsened throughout HIIT.
source: Indeed, quantification of the number of times a mouse landed on the shock grid at the bottom of the treadmill revealed a significant increase in occurrences by MyomakerscKO 8w mice, which progressively worsened throughout HIIT (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B quantifying shock grid visits.

claim: Single EDL myofibers revealed similar numbers of nuclei between MyomakerscKO 8w sedentary and HIIT mice, indicating that myonuclear accretion was effectively blocked.
source: Single EDL myofibers revealed similar numbers of nuclei between MyomakerscKO 8w sedentary and HIIT mice, indicating that myonuclear accretion was effectively blocked (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Analysis of muscle weights indicated no increase in size of multiple muscle groups between MyomakerscKO 8w sedentary and HIIT mice.
source: Analysis of muscle weights indicated no increase in size of multiple muscle groups between MyomakerscKO 8w sedentary and HIIT mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: MyomakerscKO 8w mice did not undergo hypertrophy after 8 weeks of HIIT in the gastrocnemius.
source: Moreover, histological examination of the gastrocnemius and quadriceps revealed that MyomakerscKO 8w mice did not undergo hypertrophy after 8 weeks of HIIT (Figure 3C). Quantification of myofiber CSA confirmed a lack of HIIT-induced hypertrophy in MyomakerscKO 8w mice (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claim: MyomakerscKO 8w mice did not undergo hypertrophy after 8 weeks of HIIT in the quadriceps.
source: Moreover, histological examination of the gastrocnemius and quadriceps revealed that MyomakerscKO 8w mice did not undergo hypertrophy after 8 weeks of HIIT (Figure 3C). Quantification of myofiber CSA confirmed a lack of HIIT-induced hypertrophy in MyomakerscKO 8w mice (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claim: A reduction of CSA was observed in the quadriceps, but not gastrocnemius, of MyomakerscKO 8w sedentary mice suggesting a potential role for MP fusion during homeostasis.
source: Of note, we did observe a reduction of CSA in the quadriceps, but not gastrocnemius, of MyomakerscKO 8w sedentary mice suggesting a potential role for MP fusion during homeostasis.
evidence: This claim is based on observations from the experimental data and includes speculative reasoning about the role of MP fusion.

claim: MyomakerscKO 8w HIIT mice did not display an increase in strength compared to MyomakerscKO 8w sedentary mice.
source: Finally, we also performed in vivo plantar flexion functional analysis and MyomakerscKO 8w HIIT mice did not display an increase in strength compared to MyomakerscKO 8w sedentary mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Loss of MP fusogenicity at the onset of HIIT results in exercise intolerance and a failure of the muscle to properly adapt.
source: Taken together, loss of MP fusogenicity at the onset of HIIT results in exercise intolerance and a failure of the muscle to properly adapt.
evidence: This claim is a summary conclusion based on multiple experimental observations including shock grid visits, lack of hypertrophy, and lack of strength gains.

claim: Levels of creatine kinase in the serum of MyomakerscKO 8w mice were increased at 2 weeks and 4 weeks of HIIT compared to control mice.
source: Levels of creatine kinase in the serum of MyomakerscKO 8w mice were increased at 2 weeks and 4 weeks of HIIT compared to control mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A measuring serum creatine kinase.

claim: Contractile stress genes Ankrd1, Ankrd2, and Csrp3 were upregulated during HIIT in MyomakerscKO 8w mice.
source: Each of these contractile stress genes were upregulated during HIIT in MyomakerscKO 8w mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, C, and D measuring gene expression.

claim: The initial stages of HIIT led to some level of mechanical stress of the muscle, which was subsequently attenuated as part of the normal adaptive response in control mice.
source: These data indicate that the initial stages of HIIT led to some level of mechanical stress of the muscle, which was subsequently attenuated as part of the normal adaptive response in control mice.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the data showing elevated stress markers in MyomakerscKO 8w mice but not in control mice.

claim: The inability to resolve the initial mechanical stress could account for the exercise intolerance observed in MyomakerscKO 8w mice.
source: Thus, the inability to resolve the initial mechanical stress could account for the exercise intolerance observed in MyomakerscKO 8w mice.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data linking mechanical stress to exercise intolerance.

claim: Damage in MyomakerscKO 8w HIIT mice was not major enough to elicit functional deficits.
source: It should be noted that damage in MyomakerscKO 8w HIIT mice was not major enough to elicit functional deficits (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is based on the observation that muscle weights were not reduced in MyomakerscKO 8w HIIT mice.

claim: MP fusion is required to adapt to mechanical damage during the early portion of HIIT.
source: Nonetheless, MP fusion is required to adapt to mechanical damage during the early portion of HIIT, and a failure to repair this damage negatively impacts future bouts of exercise.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion based on the experimental observations in MyomakerscKO 8w mice.

claim: MyomakerscKO 4w mice showed no difference in treadmill shocks per minute compared to control mice.
source: We first tested if MyomakerscKO 4w mice were able to tolerate HIIT and found no difference in treadmill shocks per minute compared to control mice (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Control HIIT mice displayed normal muscle architecture with the absence of fibrosis.
source: Control HIIT mice also displayed normal muscle architecture with the absence of fibrosis, but MyomakerscKO 8w mice exhibited interstitial fibrosis (Figure 4C and D) indicating that loss of MP fusion early in the HIIT protocol results in maladaptive remodeling.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: MyomakerscKO 8w mice exhibited interstitial fibrosis indicating that loss of MP fusion early in the HIIT protocol results in maladaptive remodeling.
source: Control HIIT mice also displayed normal muscle architecture with the absence of fibrosis, but MyomakerscKO 8w mice exhibited interstitial fibrosis (Figure 4C and D) indicating that loss of MP fusion early in the HIIT protocol results in maladaptive remodeling.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: No fibrosis was detected in MyomakerscKO 4w mice after HIIT showing that loss of MP fusion at this stage does not impact the ability of mice to exercise or result in maladaptive remodeling.
source: In contrast, no fibrosis was detected in MyomakerscKO 4w mice after HIIT showing that loss of MP fusion at this stage does not impact the ability of mice to exercise or result in maladaptive remodeling (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: There is a direct link between loss of MP fusion in the early stages of HIIT and maladaptive remodeling.
source: Moreover, these results reveal a direct link between loss of MP fusion in the early stages of HIIT and maladaptive remodeling.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison between MyomakerscKO 8w and MyomakerscKO 4w mice.

claim: Control mice subjected to HIIT displayed a 15–20% increase in myofiber size in the gastrocnemius.
source: Analysis of myofiber size in the gastrocnemius and quadriceps of control mice subjected to HIIT displayed the expected 15–20% increase, however MyomakerscKO 4w muscle failed to hypertrophy (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: Control mice subjected to HIIT displayed a 15–20% increase in myofiber size in the quadriceps.
source: Analysis of myofiber size in the gastrocnemius and quadriceps of control mice subjected to HIIT displayed the expected 15–20% increase, however MyomakerscKO 4w muscle failed to hypertrophy (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: MyomakerscKO 4w muscle failed to hypertrophy.
source: Analysis of myofiber size in the gastrocnemius and quadriceps of control mice subjected to HIIT displayed the expected 15–20% increase, however MyomakerscKO 4w muscle failed to hypertrophy (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: A significant reduction of myonuclei was observed in MyomakerscKO 4w myofibers compared to control mice that performed HIIT.
source: Compared to control mice that performed HIIT we observed a significant reduction of myonuclei in MyomakerscKO 4w myofibers, which reached the level of myonuclei in control mice at 4 weeks of HIIT (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Further myonuclear accretion was blocked soon after the 4 week time point in MyomakerscKO 4w muscle.
source: This indicates that further myonuclear accretion was blocked soon after the 4 week time point in MyomakerscKO 4w muscle.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that MyomakerscKO 4w myofibers had similar myonuclear numbers to control mice at 4 weeks of HIIT.

claim: Larger myofibers were observed in control HIIT compared to sedentary mice but no volume increase was detected in MyomakerscKO 4w myofibers.
source: We also assessed myofiber volume in EDL myofibers and observed larger myofibers in control HIIT compared to sedentary mice but did not detect any volume increase in MyomakerscKO 4w myofibers (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: HIIT-induced muscle growth requires MP fusion throughout the exercise protocol.
source: Taken together, HIIT-induced muscle growth requires MP fusion throughout the exercise protocol.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion based on the experimental observations in MyomakerscKO 4w mice.

claim: There is a tight relationship between myonuclear numbers and adaptive growth.
source: While this indicates a tight relationship between myonuclear numbers and adaptive growth, it also raises the intriguing possibility that the mechanistic requirement for fusion at the later stages of HIIT is independent, and potentially distinct, from the need for accrual in the earlier stages that involve injury and repair.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental observations and includes speculative reasoning.

claim: The mechanistic requirement for fusion at the later stages of HIIT is potentially independent and distinct from the need for accrual in the earlier stages that involve injury and repair.
source: While this indicates a tight relationship between myonuclear numbers and adaptive growth, it also raises the intriguing possibility that the mechanistic requirement for fusion at the later stages of HIIT is independent, and potentially distinct, from the need for accrual in the earlier stages that involve injury and repair.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: Both control and MyomakerscKO myofibers display an ability to hypertrophy in response to ACVR2B-Fc treatment.
source: Histological analysis revealed an increase in myofiber size in both control and MyomakerscKO mice that received ACVR2B-Fc (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: MyomakerscKO muscle possesses the ability to grow in response to pharmacologic stimuli.
source: Assessment of muscle weights normalized to tibia length in ACVR2B-Fc-treated animals, as a percentage of their respective PBS-treated controls, also showed that MyomakerscKO muscle possesses the ability to grow in response to pharmacologic stimuli (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Muscle growth driven by myostatin inhibition in the absence of MP fusion ability further indicates that the reason underlying a lack of hypertrophy in HIIT-trained MyomakerscKO 4w muscle is due to deficient myonuclear accretion in the final stages of exercise.
source: Muscle growth driven by myostatin inhibition in the absence of MP fusion ability, further indicates that the reason underlying a lack of hypertrophy in HIIT-trained MyomakerscKO 4w muscle is due to deficient myonuclear accretion in the final stages of exercise.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison between ACVR2B-Fc-induced growth and HIIT-induced growth in MyomakerscKO mice.

claim: HIIT resulted in a 16% increase in myofiber CSA in the gastrocnemius.
source: HIIT resulted in a 16% increase in myofiber CSA in the gastrocnemius and a 21% increase in the quadriceps, which developed between 4 and 8 weeks of the protocol.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: HIIT resulted in a 21% increase in myofiber CSA in the quadriceps.
source: HIIT resulted in a 16% increase in myofiber CSA in the gastrocnemius and a 21% increase in the quadriceps, which developed between 4 and 8 weeks of the protocol.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: Absence of MP-derived Myomaker at the beginning of HIIT resulted in an inability to withstand the exercise stimulus, development of maladaptive remodeling, and lack of adaptive hypertrophy.
source: Absence of MP-derived Myomaker at the beginning of HIIT resulted in an inability to withstand the exercise stimulus, development of maladaptive remodeling, and lack of adaptive hypertrophy, whereas deletion of Myomaker 4 weeks into HIIT mainly impacted hypertrophy.
evidence: This claim is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: Deletion of Myomaker 4 weeks into HIIT mainly impacted hypertrophy.
source: Absence of MP-derived Myomaker at the beginning of HIIT resulted in an inability to withstand the exercise stimulus, development of maladaptive remodeling, and lack of adaptive hypertrophy, whereas deletion of Myomaker 4 weeks into HIIT mainly impacted hypertrophy.
evidence: This claim is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: Ablation of MuSCs with a DTA allele in 4 month-old mice was initially reported to not impact the ability for myofibers to hypertrophy after synergist ablation.
source: Ablation of MuSCs with a DTA allele in 4 month-old mice, which would inhibit the potential to generate fusogenic MPs, was initially reported to not impact the ability for myofibers to hypertrophy after synergist ablation, leading to the idea that MuSCs were dispensible (McCarthy et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to McCarthy et al., 2011.

claim: An independent group found MuSC-ablated muscle was unable to hypertrophy in 3–4 month-old-mice after synergist ablation.
source: This experiment was repeated by an independent group that antithetically found MuSC-ablated muscle was unable to hypertrophy in 3–4 month-old-mice (Egner et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Egner et al., 2016.

claim: Genetic deletion of serum response factor (Srf), which is required for fusion, confirmed the requirement of MuSCs for overload-induced hypertrophy in 3 month old mice.
source: Moreover, another study confirmed the requirement of MuSCs for overload-induced hypertrophy in 3 month old mice through genetic deletion of serum response factor (Srf), which is required for fusion (Randrianarison-Huetz et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Randrianarison-Huetz et al., 2018.

claim: Ablation of MuSCs at 4 weeks of age reduces normal developmental hypertrophy.
source: Recent evidence claims an age-dependence on MuSCs as ablation of MuSCs at 4 weeks of age reduces normal developmental hypertrophy (Bachman et al., 2018), while loss of MuSCs in the adult has minimal effects in sedentary mice (Fry et al., 2015; Keefe et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bachman et al., 2018.

claim: Loss of MuSCs in the adult has minimal effects in sedentary mice.
source: Recent evidence claims an age-dependence on MuSCs as ablation of MuSCs at 4 weeks of age reduces normal developmental hypertrophy (Bachman et al., 2018), while loss of MuSCs in the adult has minimal effects in sedentary mice (Fry et al., 2015; Keefe et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Fry et al., 2015 and Keefe et al., 2015.

claim: Ablation of MP fusion at the onset of HIIT in 8-month-old mice results in exercise intolerance and fibrosis.
source: We show here that ablation of MP fusion at the onset of HIIT in 8-month-old mice results in exercise intolerance and fibrosis.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: It is unlikely that MyomakerscKO mice at 8 months of age would be able to properly adapt to synergist ablation.
source: Since synergist ablation is a stronger stimulus compared to HIIT, we think it is unlikely that MyomakerscKO mice at 8 months of age would be able to properly adapt to synergist ablation.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the comparison between HIIT and synergist ablation.

claim: Age dependence may not sufficiently explain the discrepancy about the role of MuSCs for synergist ablation-induced hypertrophy in mice that are 3–4 months of age.
source: Overall, our data indicates that age dependence may not sufficiently explain the discrepancy about the role of MuSCs for synergist ablation-induced hypertrophy in mice that are 3–4 months of age.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and comparison with previous studies.

claim: Approximately 25 myonuclei per myofiber are added within the first 2 weeks of HIIT.
source: Myonuclear accretion during HIIT is continuous where approximately 25 myonuclei per myofiber are added within the first 2 weeks, another 25–30 myonuclei between 2 and 4 weeks, and then 25 myonuclei over the final 4 weeks.
evidence: This claim is calculated from the experimental data showing myonuclear numbers at different time points.

claim: Another 25–30 myonuclei are added between 2 and 4 weeks of HIIT.
source: Myonuclear accretion during HIIT is continuous where approximately 25 myonuclei per myofiber are added within the first 2 weeks, another 25–30 myonuclei between 2 and 4 weeks, and then 25 myonuclei over the final 4 weeks.
evidence: This claim is calculated from the experimental data showing myonuclear numbers at different time points.

claim: 25 myonuclei are added over the final 4 weeks of HIIT.
source: Myonuclear accretion during HIIT is continuous where approximately 25 myonuclei per myofiber are added within the first 2 weeks, another 25–30 myonuclei between 2 and 4 weeks, and then 25 myonuclei over the final 4 weeks.
evidence: This claim is calculated from the experimental data showing myonuclear numbers at different time points.

claim: Myonuclear accretion precedes detectable growth during HIIT.
source: While myonuclear number increases throughout HIIT, growth of myofibers occurred between 4 and 8 weeks indicating that myonuclear accretion precedes detectable growth.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the temporal relationship between myonuclear accretion and hypertrophy.

claim: Myofibers acquire new nuclei before an increase in size in response to synergist ablation.
source: This is consistent with the response of muscle to synergist ablation where myofibers acquire new nuclei before an increase in size (Bruusgaard et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bruusgaard et al., 2010.

claim: Ablation of Myomaker in MPs 4 weeks after HIIT resulted in a failure to hypertrophy even though this only corresponds to a lack of 25 myonuclei.
source: Ablation of Myomaker in MPs 4 weeks after HIIT resulted in a failure to hypertrophy even though this only corresponds to a lack of 25 myonuclei.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental data and calculations from myonuclear counts.

claim: The addition of 50–55 myonuclei added during the initial 4 weeks of HIIT are not sufficient to drive adaptive hypertrophy.
source: These data show that the addition of 50–55 myonuclei added during the initial 4 weeks of HIIT are not sufficient to drive adaptive hypertrophy.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that MyomakerscKO 4w mice failed to hypertrophy despite having accumulated 50-55 myonuclei.

claim: HIIT-induced adaptive growth requires continued myonuclear accrual throughout the protocol.
source: Thus, a key finding from our work is that HIIT-induced adaptive growth requires continued myonuclear accrual throughout the protocol.
evidence: This is a key conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: The HIIT protocol may have uncoupled adaptive processes (mitigation of injury and growth) since there are multiple lines of evidence suggesting distinct phases during HIIT.
source: Surprisingly, the HIIT protocol described here may have uncoupled these adaptive processes since there are multiple lines of evidence suggesting distinct phases (mitigation of injury and growth) during HIIT.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: Muscle damage is a normal response to HIIT and these damage markers progressively diminish over the duration of the protocol.
source: First, we show that muscle damage (assessed by levels of serum creatine kinase and contractile stress genes) is a normal response to HIIT and these damage markers progressively diminish over the duration of the protocol.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental data measuring creatine kinase and stress gene expression.

claim: If fusion is abrogated at the onset of HIIT (MyomakerscKO 8w), mice are unable to repair HIIT-induced muscle damage, which causes exercise intolerance.
source: If fusion is abrogated at the onset of HIIT (MyomakerscKO 8w), mice are unable to repair HIIT-induced muscle damage, which causes exercise intolerance.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental observations in MyomakerscKO 8w mice.

claim: When mice are allowed to accumulate new nuclei into the myofiber (approximately 50–55) during the first four weeks but further MP fusion is blocked (MyomakerscKO 4w), the mice are able to exercise normally indicating that the damage phase of exercise has been mitigated.
source: However, when mice are allowed to accumulate new nuclei into the myofiber (approximately 50–55) during the first four weeks but further MP fusion is blocked (MyomakerscKO 4w), the mice are able to exercise normally indicating that the damage phase of exercise has been mitigated.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental observations in MyomakerscKO 4w mice.

claim: Resistance training causes early increases in protein synthesis to support tissue repair but does not correlate with hypertrophy, which occurs only after the repair of damage in humans.
source: These data are generally consistent with reports in humans that resistance training causes early increases in protein synthesis to support tissue repair but does not correlate with hypertrophy, which occurs only after the repair of damage (Damas et al., 2016; Mitchell et al., 2014; Moore et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Damas et al., 2016; Mitchell et al., 2014; and Moore et al., 2005.

claim: The nature of the stimulus changed from a gradual increase in treadmill incline in the first four weeks to an increase in speed (with constant incline) over the next four weeks.

claim: MyomakerscKO 8w mice exhibit progressive failure to exercise even after the protocol changed.
source: One argument against this possibility is that MyomakerscKO 8w mice exhibit progressive failure to exercise even after the protocol changed.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental observations.

claim: Nuclei added during the first four weeks of HIIT still support the reparative response in the final four weeks of HIIT, which allows MyomakerscKO 4w mice to tolerate the exercise.
source: Another possibility that could explain the ability for MyomakerscKO 4w mice to exercise is that nuclei added during the first four weeks of HIIT still support the reparative response in the final four weeks of HIIT, which allows them to tolerate the exercise.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: There is a tight correlation between absolute myonuclear numbers and growth potential, with minimal tolerance for reduced numbers.
source: Perhaps there is a tight correlation between absolute myonuclear numbers and growth potential, with minimal tolerance for reduced numbers.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: The 25 new myonuclei added in the final 4 weeks of HIIT are specialized for growth whereas the 50–55 myonuclei added in the first 4 weeks of HIIT are mainly utilized for repair of tissue injury.
source: In this scenario, the 25 new myonuclei added in the final 4 weeks of HIIT are specialized for growth whereas the 50–55 myonuclei added in the first 4 weeks of HIIT are mainly utilized for repair of tissue injury.

claim: There is a potential lack of redundancy within the population of the newly accrued nuclei, given the apparent inability of the 50–55 nuclei added early in HIIT to compensate for the lack of 25 nuclei late in HIIT to drive growth.
source: Adding support to such an idea of specialized roles of accrued myonuclei is that our data also reveal a potential lack of redundancy within the population of the newly accrued nuclei, given the apparent inability of the 50–55 nuclei added early in HIIT to compensate for the lack of 25 nuclei late in HIIT to drive growth.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations.

claim: It is possible that there is a tight correlation of myonuclear number for growth because new nuclei specialized for growth are required, thereby increasing overall myonuclear numbers.
source: More specifically, it is possible that there is a tight correlation of myonuclear number for growth because new nuclei specialized for growth are required, thereby increasing overall myonuclear numbers.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation attempting to reconcile different hypotheses.

claim: The myonuclear domain theory postulates that a given myonucleus controls a certain volume of cytoplasm.
source: The importance of myonuclear accretion has classically been viewed through the lens of the myonuclear domain theory, which postulates that a given myonucleus controls a certain volume of cytoplasm (Murach et al., 2018b), and that for muscle to grow it needs more nuclei to support the larger cellular volume.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Murach et al., 2018b.

claim: The myonuclear domain theory may be too simplistic to explain the complexity of muscle adaptability.
source: We propose that the myonuclear domain theory may be too simplistic to explain the complexity of muscle adaptability.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the experimental findings.

claim: A major issue with the myonuclear domain theory is that it links myonuclear numbers solely with growth.
source: A major issue with the myonuclear domain theory is that it links myonuclear numbers solely with growth.
evidence: This is a critical interpretation of existing theory.

claim: The myonuclear domain theory assumes all myonuclei, freshly accrued or added during development, are homogenous in terms of both magnitude and profile of transcriptional activity.
source: In doing so, it assumes all myonuclei, freshly accrued or added during development, are homogenous in terms of both magnitude and profile of transcriptional activity.
evidence: This is an inference about the assumptions underlying the myonuclear domain theory.

claim: Myonuclei possess the ability to alter transcription in the absence of MuSCs suggesting a dynamic, heterogenous system.
source: However, myonuclei possess the ability to alter transcription in the absence of MuSCs suggesting a dynamic, heterogenous system (Kirby et al., 2016b).

claim: Myonuclear accrual extends beyond just the maintenance of the myonuclear domain.
source: Our data reveals that myonuclear accrual extends beyond just the maintenance of the myonuclear domain.

claim: MP fusion and myonuclear accrual are essential for normal exercise-related adaptive responses that encompass both repair and growth.
source: Indeed, MP fusion and myonuclear accrual are essential for normal exercise-related adaptive responses that encompass both repair and growth, which has implications for maintaining muscle mass during disease and aging.
evidence: This is a key conclusion of the study.

claim: In 8 month-old mice, HIIT led to progressive myonuclear accretion throughout the protocol, and functional muscle hypertrophy.
source: In 8 month-old mice, HIIT led to progressive myonuclear accretion throughout the protocol, and functional muscle hypertrophy.

evidence: This is a summary statement from the abstract based on experimental findings.

claim: Myonuclear accretion is required for different facets of exercise-induced adaptive responses, impacting both muscle repair and hypertrophic growth.
source: We conclude that myonuclear accretion is required for different facets of exercise-induced adaptive responses, impacting both muscle repair and hypertrophic growth.

claim: Myomaker (Mymk) is a muscle-specific factor required for fusion.
source: Through a complementary approach, we abrogated MP fusion by genetically deleting Myomaker (Mymk), a muscle-specific factor required for fusion, and found that synergist ablation-induced hypertrophy was significantly blunted (Goh and Millay, 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to previous work.

claim: Myostatin is a negative regulator of muscle mass.
source: To address this concern, we employed a pharmacologic approach to drive hypertrophy through manipulation of myostatin signaling, which is a negative regulator of muscle mass (Lee, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lee, 2004.
